summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcohol dependence, alcoholic cirrhosis, portal hypertension, esophageal varices, and asthma was admitted for abdominal pain and alcohol withdrawal following a relapse involving daily consumption of brandy. He presented with epigastric and right upper quadrant pain radiating to the back, tremulousness, and anxiety. He was managed with CIWA-guided diazepam tapering, restarted on home medications including nadolol, spironolactone, omeprazole, and lactulose, and treated for pain with acetaminophen, tramadol, and hydromorphone. His withdrawal symptoms resolved, liver enzymes improved, and abdominal pain decreased during the hospitalization. Social work engaged him in counseling, and plans were made to restart Suboxone and follow up with primary care and addiction services. He was discharged home in stable condition with clear instructions on abstinence, medication adherence, and follow-up.
problems: Esophageal varices in diseases classified elsewhere, without mention of bleeding
